correctness.rationale: Each representation x+y=s, x^-1+y^-1=t gives t=s/(xy), so valuations agree and zero pair has exactly U=(q-1)q^(k-1) roots. At common valuation a>=1, solve x²-sx+s_a/t_a=0 modulo pi^(k-a); unit discriminant square iff -s_a/t_a is square in residue field, by odd-characteristic Hensel two roots each with q^a lifts. At unit s,t the discriminant D=s²-4s/t is zero (q^floor(k/2) solutions) or has even valuation 2j<k and square unit part (2q^j roots), else none. For fixed unit s, t->D bijects units with elements not congruent to s² mod pi; splitting the square residue/zero-discriminant and higher valuation sets gives disjoint histogram families. Squaring counts yields E=3(q-1)q^(2k-2)[k(q-1)-1], Fourier Parseval factor q^(2k), and geometric sums yield stated support and asymptotic density. Independently enumerated cyclic moduli 3,9,27,25,125: E=6,162,2430,2100,82500 and support 3,9,57,129,3009 match formula; inspected code additionally treats dual numbers and F9[epsilon]. No finite enumeration is used in place of the Hensel proof.
residual_risks: Odd residue characteristic, commutative principal chain ideals and ordered convolution are essential; no even characteristic, general local ring, higher fold or sharp weighted extension result.

originality.rationale: Kowalski 2010 already discusses the field-level symmetric-sum/Kloosterman fourth moment; Gong–Veys–Wan 2013 provides aggregate moments for classical prime-power cyclic rings and the present energy should not be separately advertised as a new fourth-moment phenomenon. Bower–Evans–Luo–Miller concerns one-coordinate sum/difference sets of hyperbola points, distinct from planar H+H. The assigned claim adds the entire pointwise valuation and square-class distribution, disjoint multiplicity strata and support density uniformly across all odd finite commutative chain rings including noncyclic rings, not established by those prior results as inspected.
residual_risks: Older local congruence/Kloosterman literature could contain equivalent chain-ring square-root stratification; aggregate energy in cyclic rings definitely has strong prior coverage, only pointwise all-chain-ring classification assessed as original.
